title: Hosts overview
description: arnor, gondor and shire, sampled over SSH every 5 minutes by gadget-monitor.

panels.title: CPU utilization
panels.description: Average busy % across all cores (everything except idle and iowait), averaged over each sample interval.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: 1-minute (solid) and 5-minute (dashed) load averages. Compare with core counts: arnor 256, gondor 128, shire 32.

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: Load average divided by online CPUs; around 1.0 means every core has work queued.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Used (solid) is total minus available: memory new work can't have without swapping, so page cache the kernel would give back doesn't count. Total (dashed) is installed RAM; the gap between the two is what is still available.

panels.title: Direct reclaim stalls
panels.description: Times per second a memory allocation stalled to reclaim memory itself (allocstall, all zones, from /proc/vmstat). It slows whatever process is allocating, even while memory available looks fine. 0 is normal.

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: Swap in use (solid) against total swap (dashed); the gap is what is free. gondor has no swap configured, so both are 0.

panels.title: Swap free now
panels.description: Percent of swap still free. 'no swap' means the host has none configured.

panels.title: Root filesystem (/) used
panels.description: Space used on / (solid) against the filesystem's size (dashed); the disk is full where the lines meet. Used is size minus what ordinary users can still write, so the gap is exactly the space left. The operating system, /var and /tmp live here.

panels.title: /local used
panels.description: Space used on /local (solid) against the filesystem's size (dashed); the disk is full where the lines meet. Used is size minus what ordinary users can still write, so the gap is exactly the space left. Local scratch space for users and services.

panels.title: Disk used now
panels.description: Percent of each local filesystem in use (/ and /local; shire's exported filesystems are on the NFS server dashboard).

panels.title: Login time
panels.description: Time for a brand-new interactive SSH login to reach a usable shell, probed every 5 minutes (every 15 after repeated timeouts). Timeouts (60 s) show as FAIL on ssh_login in Check status.

panels.title: Login stages: $login_host
panels.description: Where the login time goes, stacked. connect: DNS and TCP. auth: key exchange and authentication, which on these hosts reads ~/.ssh/authorized_keys from the NFS home directory. shell: session setup, login shell and profile until a typed command runs. A hung login shows only the stages it finished.

panels.title: Conda startup time
panels.description: Time to activate a conda environment, start its python3 and import the packages in checks/conda.sh (lsdb), in a clean shell, probed every 5 minutes. The same environment is installed in three locations: shire (solid), shiren (dotted) and astro-gadget's home directory on helios (dashed). A location that fails or takes over 60 s has no point here.

panels.title: Conda startup stages, shire: $conda_host
panels.description: Where the startup time goes for the environment on shire, stacked. activate: source conda.sh and conda activate (this runs conda's own Python, from the same location). python: start the environment's python3 and print. import: import each package, in one interpreter. A location that hangs shows only the stages it finished.

panels.title: Conda startup stages, shiren: $conda_host
panels.description: Where the startup time goes for the environment on shiren, stacked. activate: source conda.sh and conda activate (this runs conda's own Python, from the same location). python: start the environment's python3 and print. import: import each package, in one interpreter. A location that hangs shows only the stages it finished.

panels.title: Conda startup stages, home: $conda_host
panels.description: Where the startup time goes for the environment on home, stacked. activate: source conda.sh and conda activate (this runs conda's own Python, from the same location). python: start the environment's python3 and print. import: import each package, in one interpreter. A location that hangs shows only the stages it finished.

panels.title: Queue wait per call: helios
panels.description: Average time an NFS call to helios waited in the client before being sent, over all operations, from the kernel's per-mount counters. Rising queue wait means the client has more requests than it can put on the wire (or the server is slow to free slots).

targets.expr: sum by (host) (rate(gadget_nfs_queue_seconds_total{host=~"$host", fs="helios"}[$__interval])) / sum by (host) (rate(gadget_nfs_ops_total{host=~"$host", fs="helios"}[$__interval]))

panels.title: Round-trip time per call: helios
panels.description: Average time from sending an NFS call to helios until its reply arrived (network plus server), over all operations. Calls still in progress are not counted until they finish, so a hung server shows as a gap, not a spike.

targets.expr: sum by (host) (rate(gadget_nfs_rtt_seconds_total{host=~"$host", fs="helios"}[$__interval])) / sum by (host) (rate(gadget_nfs_ops_total{host=~"$host", fs="helios"}[$__interval]))

panels.description: Average time from sending an NFS call to shire until its reply arrived (network plus server), over all operations. Calls still in progress are not counted until they finish, so a hung server shows as a gap, not a spike.

targets.expr: sum by (host) (rate(gadget_nfs_rtt_seconds_total{host=~"$host", fs="shire"}[$__interval])) / sum by (host) (rate(gadget_nfs_ops_total{host=~"$host", fs="shire"}[$__interval]))

panels.title: Stuck processes, NFS state and RDMA
Processes in D state
panels.description: Processes in uninterruptible sleep (state D), sampled every minute. These are usually waiting on I/O, often NFS, and can't be killed until it completes. A few for a moment is normal; a count that stays up means something is stuck. This was the first visible symptom of the November 2026 outage (hung Jupyter kernels).

panels.title: NFS state manager threads
panels.description: NFSv4 client kernel threads ("<server>-manager") recovering lease or delegation state, sampled every minute. Normally 0: one appears briefly when a server asks for state back. Present at sample after sample means recovery is looping, as in the November 2026 outage.

panels.title: TEST_STATEID share of NFS calls
panels.description: TEST_STATEID calls as a percent of all NFS calls to helios, shire and shiren. The client sends TEST_STATEID to check whether state it holds is still valid after the server revoked some. Normally near 0; above a few percent is abnormal. In the November 2026 outage it was 81% of all NFSv4 calls.

panels.title: TEST_STATEID calls
panels.description: TEST_STATEID calls per second, per host and NFS filesystem (helios solid, shire dashed, shiren dotted).

panels.title: DELEGRETURN calls
panels.description: Delegations handed back to the server, per second, per host and filesystem (helios solid, shire dashed, shiren dotted). A delegation lets a client cache a file; it returns one when done or when the server recalls it. A sustained high rate is delegation churn, which preceded the November 2026 outage. Their queue wait is on 'Queue wait by operation'.

panels.title: RDMA port state
panels.description: State of each RDMA (RoCE) port, from /sys/class/infiniband. NFS to shire runs over RoCE. Disabled (gray) is a port whose link is disabled, normally because it isn't cabled: mlx5_1 on arnor and gondor. shire has one port, the bond mlx5_bond_0. Any other port that isn't ACTIVE is a problem.

targets.expr: max by (host, device, port) (node_infiniband_state_id{host=~"$host"} unless on (host, device, port) node_infiniband_physical_state_id{host=~"$host"} == 3) or max by (host, device, port) (node_infiniband_physical_state_id{host=~"$host"} == 3) * 0 - 1

panels.title: RDMA errors and retransmissions: $host
panels.description: Events per second from the RDMA adapters' hardware counters, all ports summed; only counters that moved in the time range are drawn, and a green "no errors" line at 0 when none did. packet_seq_err and out_of_sequence: packets lost or reordered. local_ack_timeout_err: a peer didn't acknowledge in time. roce_adp_retrans and roce_slow_restart_cnps: retransmissions and congestion slow-downs. *_remote_access_errors and *_cqe_error: failed operations. The November 2026 outage showed hundreds of thousands of sequence errors and retransmissions.

targets.expr: sum by (counter) (rate(gadget_rdma_hw_counter_total{host="$host", counter=~"packet_seq_err|out_of_sequence|local_ack_timeout_err|roce_adp_retrans|roce_slow_restart_cnps|req_remote_access_errors|req_cqe_error|resp_cqe_error"}[$__interval])) and on (counter) (sum by (counter) (increase(gadget_rdma_hw_counter_total{host="$host", counter=~"packet_seq_err|out_of_sequence|local_ack_timeout_err|roce_adp_retrans|roce_slow_restart_cnps|req_remote_access_errors|req_cqe_error|resp_cqe_error"}[$__range] @ end())) > 0)

panels.title: Queue wait by operation: $nfs_host, helios
panels.description: Average client-side queue wait per call to helios, per NFS operation. OPEN includes OPEN_NOATTR; OTHER is every remaining operation (DELEGRETURN, SETATTR, RENAME, READDIR, LOCK, COMMIT, ...). A line has gaps while that operation had no calls.

targets.expr: sum by (op) (label_replace(rate(gadget_nfs_queue_seconds_total{host="$nfs_host", fs="helios"}[$__interval]), "op", "OTHER", "op", "TEST_STATEID|FREE_STATEID")) / sum by (op) (label_replace(rate(gadget_nfs_ops_total{host="$nfs_host", fs="helios"}[$__interval]), "op", "OTHER", "op", "TEST_STATEID|FREE_STATEID"))

panels.title: Queue wait by operation: $nfs_host, shire
panels.description: Average client-side queue wait per call to shire, per NFS operation. OPEN includes OPEN_NOATTR; OTHER is every remaining operation (DELEGRETURN, SETATTR, RENAME, READDIR, LOCK, COMMIT, ...). A line has gaps while that operation had no calls.

targets.expr: sum by (op) (label_replace(rate(gadget_nfs_queue_seconds_total{host="$nfs_host", fs="shire"}[$__interval]), "op", "OTHER", "op", "TEST_STATEID|FREE_STATEID")) / sum by (op) (label_replace(rate(gadget_nfs_ops_total{host="$nfs_host", fs="shire"}[$__interval]), "op", "OTHER", "op", "TEST_STATEID|FREE_STATEID"))

panels.title: Queue wait by operation: $nfs_host, shiren
panels.description: Average client-side queue wait per call to shiren, per NFS operation. OPEN includes OPEN_NOATTR; OTHER is every remaining operation (DELEGRETURN, SETATTR, RENAME, READDIR, LOCK, COMMIT, ...). A line has gaps while that operation had no calls.

targets.expr: sum by (op) (label_replace(rate(gadget_nfs_queue_seconds_total{host="$nfs_host", fs="shiren"}[$__interval]), "op", "OTHER", "op", "TEST_STATEID|FREE_STATEID")) / sum by (op) (label_replace(rate(gadget_nfs_ops_total{host="$nfs_host", fs="shiren"}[$__interval]), "op", "OTHER", "op", "TEST_STATEID|FREE_STATEID"))

panels.title: GPU memory used
panels.description: GPU memory in use (solid, total minus the driver's free figure) against each GPU's total (dashed), sampled every minute. The driver keeps about 0.6 GB per GPU for itself, so used never quite drops to 0.

panels.title: GPU utilization
panels.description: Percent of time a GPU kernel was running, from the driver's samples over the ~14 s before each once-a-minute check: average (solid) and peak (dashed). Covers about a quarter of the time, so short bursts between checks can be missed.

panels.title: GPU processes
panels.description: Number of processes holding each GPU (they may hold memory without computing).

panels.title: Users per day
panels.description: Distinct users on the selected hosts in each day (Pacific time; the last bar is the day so far). Logged in: had at least one process running. Active: in at least one 5-minute interval, used 2+ CPU cores on average, or held 5+ GiB of RAM, or kept a GPU 5%+ busy, or held 1+ GiB of GPU memory. root, jhub-admin, the monitor's own accounts and system accounts are not counted.

targets.expr: count(max by (user) (max_over_time(((max by (host, user) (max_over_time(gadget_user_processes{host=~"$host"}[5m])) > 0))[1d:5m] offset -1d))) and on() (hour(time() + timezone_offset("America/Los_Angeles")) == 0)

count(max by (user) (max_over_time(((max by (host, user) (rate(gadget_user_cpu_seconds_total{host=~"$host"}[5m])) >= 2 or max by (host, user) (max_over_time(gadget_user_memory_bytes{host=~"$host"}[5m])) >= 5368709120 or max by (host, user) (avg_over_time(gadget_user_gpu_percent{host=~"$host"}[5m])) >= 5 or max by (host, user) (max_over_time(gadget_user_gpu_memory_bytes{host=~"$host"}[5m])) >= 1073741824))[1d:5m] offset -1d))) and on() (hour(time() + timezone_offset("America/Los_Angeles")) == 0)

panels.title: Users per week
panels.description: Distinct users on the selected hosts in each week (Pacific time, weeks start Monday; the last bar is the week so far). Logged in: had at least one process running. Active: in at least one 5-minute interval, used 2+ CPU cores on average, or held 5+ GiB of RAM, or kept a GPU 5%+ busy, or held 1+ GiB of GPU memory. root, jhub-admin, the monitor's own accounts and system accounts are not counted.

targets.expr: count(max by (user) (max_over_time(((max by (host, user) (max_over_time(gadget_user_processes{host=~"$host"}[5m])) > 0))[7d:5m] offset -7d))) and on() (hour(time() + timezone_offset("America/Los_Angeles")) == 0 and on() day_of_week(time() + timezone_offset("America/Los_Angeles")) == 1)

count(max by (user) (max_over_time(((max by (host, user) (rate(gadget_user_cpu_seconds_total{host=~"$host"}[5m])) >= 2 or max by (host, user) (max_over_time(gadget_user_memory_bytes{host=~"$host"}[5m])) >= 5368709120 or max by (host, user) (avg_over_time(gadget_user_gpu_percent{host=~"$host"}[5m])) >= 5 or max by (host, user) (max_over_time(gadget_user_gpu_memory_bytes{host=~"$host"}[5m])) >= 1073741824))[7d:5m] offset -7d))) and on() (hour(time() + timezone_offset("America/Los_Angeles")) == 0 and on() day_of_week(time() + timezone_offset("America/Los_Angeles")) == 1)
